title: fix(metadata-protocol): duplicatePackage reports a refused install of the copy's package record
body:
Fixes #24041

Clause-②: no (narrowing)

## What changed (ruling B, claim amendment 6227008947)

`duplicatePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) installs the copy's package record through `installPackage` before it copies any item. That call sat in a bare `catch {}`. Now, when the install is refused, the duplicate is refused with that refusal, rethrown unchanged, before any item is copied. Nothing is minted or copied, and the door answers the refusal's own status:

- **`422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`**, with the registry's sentence and remedy ("Choose a different namespace for …"), when another installed package owns the copy's namespace (ADR-0048 Phase 1, the install-time gate in `SchemaRegistry.installPackage`). That covers an explicit `targetNamespace` and one derived from the last segment of `targetPackageId`.
- **`500`**, the install's own sentence, when the `sys_packages` write fails.

The refusal is logged once at `warn` by `[protocol.duplicatePackage]`, naming the target id, the source id, and the refusal's code and message, because neither the primitive nor the HTTP door logs it (measured below). For a store fault the error itself is attached to the log line, since the driver's text survives only on its `cause`. A client refusal is not attached; its sentence is already the whole story.

This keeps the rule the sibling verb `importUnmanagedPackage` states: "There is no half-copied app." The first round of this PR (a `failed[]` entry of type `package` on a duplicate that still copied) is retired: that partial state is what the ruling removes.

Also in `duplicatePackage`: the method docblock gains one sentence (the package record is not an item; its refusal refuses the whole duplicate), and comment ① of the target-id note is rewritten for the rethrow. Two test comments beside it (`protocol.duplicate-package-target-namespace.test.ts`, `protocol.install-manifest-id.test.ts`) are corrected the same way.

## Premises, measured before any edit (at `cfa01c279`)

1. **No mutation precedes the install call.** Code read of every call from the method head to the install: an organization-scope refusal and two declaration parses (throws only), `registry.getPackage` (read), `findEnvironmentRows('sys_metadata', …)` (`engine.find` plus the legacy-row read, both reads), and in-memory `Map`s. Measured with a one-off probe (not committed) over the real `ObjectKernel`, `ObjectQLPlugin` and `SchemaRegistry`, an instrumented in-memory driver, and a source holding an object and a view. A snapshot of every driver store, the package records, the namespace owners, the object contributors and the metadata keys was identical before the duplicate, at `installPackage` entry, and right after the refused install, for both refusals. Zero driver writes before the install and zero during the refused install. So no rollback is needed.
2. **The door maps the status.** A one-off probe (not committed) drove the real `HttpDispatcher.handlePackages` for `POST /:id/duplicate` over a real `SchemaRegistry`, with `duplicatePackage` throwing the exact objects the real `installPackage` throws. The namespace conflict answered `422` with `error.code` `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` and the registry's full sentence, remedy included. The store fault answered `500` `INTERNAL_ERROR` with the primitive's own sentence, which quotes only the package id. The door's `catch` is `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`). Neither the door nor the primitive logged either refusal.
3. **No caller relies on the partial copy.** objectui at the pinned `.objectui-sha` `f8267df93`: `packages-io.ts` `duplicatePackage` throws `readEnvelopeFailureText(payload)` on any non-OK answer (lines 278-289), and both callers show the thrown message: `PackagesPage.tsx` 584-588 (an error banner) and `BuilderLanding.tsx` 140-141 (`setDupErr`). Studio sends no `targetNamespace`, so from Studio the conflict comes only through a derived namespace. In this repo, the SDK's `client.packages.duplicate` goes through `unwrapResponse`, and the dogfood duplicate (`package-first-authoring.dogfood.test.ts`) duplicates a source with no registry record, so it never reaches the install call.

## Refusals a duplicate can reach

| Refusal | Raised by | Reachable from a duplicate? |
|---|---|---|
| Namespace conflict, `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, 422 | `SchemaRegistry.installPackage`'s namespace gate | **Yes.** The HTTP door forwards `targetNamespace` verbatim. Reached by an explicit namespace another package owns, or a derived one equal to another package's namespace, the source's own included. `OS_METADATA_COLLISION=warn` downgrades it to a warning, and the duplicate then proceeds. |
| `sys_packages` write failed, 500 | `installPackage` (`packagePersistFailureError`, after its undo) | Yes, on a store fault. |
| Manifest id | `installPackage`'s id leg | No. `duplicatePackage` parses `targetPackageId` with the same declaration first. |
| ADR-0087 D1 handshake | `assertProtocolCompat` | Not in practice: the copy carries the source record's `engines`, which this runtime already admitted. |
| Security catalog or default record page conflict | the registry's other install judges | Not over HTTP: they read manifest collections a base's manifest cannot carry. |
| A code or marketplace source | the runtime door's `requireDuplicableSource` | Refused 422 before the protocol is called. |

## Pins

`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.duplicate-package-install-refusal.test.ts`, three cases:
1. **The registry's namespace refusal.** `SchemaRegistry` cannot be imported here, because `@objectstack/objectql` depends on this package. So the harness registry refuses exactly when another package owns the namespace, throwing `NamespaceConflictError`'s envelope (`code`, `status` 422, its sentence), and the real `installPackage` meets it. It asserts that the duplicate rejects with that very object (`toBe`), that `resolveThrownHttpError` resolves it to `422` and `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`, that `saveMetaItem` was never called, that no target record exists and the namespace owners are unchanged, and that one warn line names the target id, the code and the sentence, with no error object attached.
2. **A failed `sys_packages` write**, with no stub on the install path. The `package` service answers `{ success: false, driverFault }`, and the real primitive undoes its registry write and throws its 500. It asserts the rejection resolves to `500`, its message names the target and quotes nothing of the store, nothing was copied, the target record is gone, and the one warn line carries the error itself, whose `cause` holds the driver text.
3. **CONTROL.** An accepted install still copies (`success: true`, the item copied as `leave_copy_ticket`) and logs no refusal.

The real-registry measurements are the premise probes above. They are cited, not kept as tests: they sit outside the claimed file surface, and the dependency cycle keeps them out of this package.

The pin read `Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3)`: both refusal cases failed with `Error: expected the duplicate to be refused, but it resolved`, and the CONTROL stayed green. The restore is proven: blob equals HEAD (`bf8238167aba`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the marker count is 0. Predicted direction red, observed red. The test imports the source by relative path, so no `dist/` leg applies.

## Acceptance notes

- When the source id has no registry record (`srcPkg` undefined), the install is skipped without a word, and that copy has no package record. The runtime door's `requireDuplicableSource` passes an unknown id on. This is outside the card by the claim; not measured; noted, not filed. Carrier: none.
